title: Hilbert-Schmidt norm: transposition invariance and the two-sided operator-ideal bounds
statement: For all natural numbers m, k, p, write R^m = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m) (Rn m) with standard basis e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1. For a continuous linear X : R^m -> R^k let hsNormSq X = sum_{i<m} |X e_i|^2. Let <.,.> be the Euclidean inner product and ||.|| the operator norm. Then: (H1) if X : R^m -> R^k and Y : R^k -> R^m are continuous linear maps with <X u, v> = <u, Y v> for all u in R^m and v in R^k (i.e. Y is an adjoint of X), then hsNormSq Y = hsNormSq X; (H2) for continuous linear Y : R^k -> R^p and X : R^m -> R^k, hsNormSq (Y o X) <= ||Y||^2 hsNormSq X; (H3) for continuous linear X : R^m -> R^k and W : R^p -> R^m, hsNormSq (X o W) <= ||W||^2 hsNormSq X.
lean_statement: (∀ (m k : ℕ) (X : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k) (Y : Rn k →L[ℝ] Rn m), (∀ (u : Rn m) (v : Rn k), inner ℝ (X u) v = inner ℝ u (Y v)) → hsNormSq Y = hsNormSq X) ∧ (∀ (m k p : ℕ) (Y : Rn k →L[ℝ] Rn p) (X : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k), hsNormSq (Y ∘L X) ≤ ‖Y‖ ^ 2 * hsNormSq X) ∧ ∀ (m k p : ℕ) (X : Rn m →L[ℝ] Rn k) (W : Rn p →L[ℝ] Rn m), hsNormSq (X ∘L W) ≤ ‖W‖ ^ 2 * hsNormSq X
